```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
    collapse = TRUE,
    comment = "#>"
)
options(ABCatlas.download_progress = FALSE)
```

The [Allen Brain Cell (ABC) Atlas][abc-atlas] publishes single-cell,
single-nucleus and spatial transcriptomics data for the mouse and human
brain, including the whole mouse brain atlases of Yao et al. [-@yao2023]
and Zhang et al. [-@zhang2023]. The Allen Institute distributes these data
through a public cloud bucket together with a Python package,
`abc_atlas_access`, for discovering and downloading files.

`r Biocpkg("ABCatlas")` provides the same access directly in R, with no Python
installation. It assembles validated cell and gene metadata for each curated
dataset, selects cells and genes, reports the size of a request before
anything is transferred, and reads only the selected cells and genes into a
sparse matrix, a `r Biocpkg("SingleCellExperiment")` or a
`r Biocpkg("SpatialExperiment")`.

The workflow has four steps:

1.  `list_datasets()` lists the curated dataset routes.
2.  `load_data()` downloads and assembles cell and gene metadata.
3.  `plan_fetch()` previews the expression files a request needs.
4.  `fetch_data()` downloads those files once and reads the selection.

[abc-atlas]: https://portal.brain-map.org/atlases-and-data/bkp/abc-atlas

# Installation

Install the package from Bioconductor:

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("ABCatlas")
```

Then load it:

```{r library}
library(ABCatlas)
```

`ABCatlas` needs no Python, compiler or system libraries: HDF5 support comes
from `r Biocpkg("rhdf5")` and `r Biocpkg("Rhdf5lib")`, which bundle the HDF5
library on all platforms. It does need:

-   **internet access** to the public ABC Atlas bucket
    (`https://allen-brain-cell-atlas.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com`) the first
    time each file is used. No account is needed. Behind a proxy, set the
    `https_proxy` environment variable before starting R;
-   **disk space** for the local cache (Section
    \@ref(cache-location-and-releases)).

# Available datasets

`list_datasets()` describes the curated dataset routes supported by the
package. It reads the package registry only and performs no network access.

```{r list-datasets}
datasets <- list_datasets()
datasets
```

Each route reports its modality, whether it is spatial or imputed, and its
expression representations. `default_data_type` is the representation used
when `data_type` is not given; `available_data_types` lists every
representation the ABC Atlas publishes for the route. These are properties of
the published data, not transformations made by `ABCatlas`: `raw` keeps
count semantics, and `log2` is transformed upstream and never presented as
counts. `MERFISH_imputed` holds expression imputed upstream; `ABCatlas`
performs no imputation.

# Loading metadata

This vignette uses `Zhuang4`, a MERFISH spatial transcriptomics dataset from
Zhang et al. [-@zhang2023] and one of the smallest routes in the atlas. Its
metadata take about 40 MB and its raw expression about 64 MB.

Files are cached in a temporary directory here, so every build of the
vignette starts from an empty cache. Section
\@ref(cache-location-and-releases) explains how to choose a permanent
location for your own analyses.

```{r cache-dir}
options(ABCatlas.download_base = file.path(tempdir(), "ABCatlas"))
abc_download_dir()
```

`load_data()` downloads and assembles the cell and gene metadata. It does not
download expression matrices.

```{r load-data}
abc <- load_data("Zhuang4")
abc
```

The result is an `abc_data` object. It keeps the dataset, release and cache
location, so it can be passed directly to `plan_fetch()` and `fetch_data()`.
Its cell metadata hold one row per cell, with anatomical, donor and taxonomy
annotations and, for this spatial route, the `x`, `y` and `z` coordinates:

```{r cell-metadata}
head(abc$cell_metadata)
```

Its gene metadata hold one row per gene, keyed by `gene_identifier`:

```{r gene-data}
head(abc$gene_data)
```

`unique_values` lists the values found in the main metadata columns, which
are the choices available for cell filters. Count them first, because some
columns are continuous:

```{r unique-values}
lengths(abc$unique_values)
lapply(abc$unique_values, head, n = 3)
```

The coordinates and the two confidence scores take almost one value per cell,
so they are not useful filter choices. The categorical columns, such as
`brain_section_label`, `neurotransmitter`, `subclass` and `cluster`, are.

# Selecting cells and genes

Cells are selected with `filters`, a named list in which each name is a cell
metadata column and each value lists the values to keep. Cells must match
every filter, and any of the values within one filter. The values below come
from the outputs above: one of the three brain sections, and the GABAergic
and glutamatergic cells in it.

```{r cell-selection}
filters <- list(
    brain_section_label = "Zhuang-ABCA-4.002",
    neurotransmitter = c("GABA", "Glut")
)
with(abc$cell_metadata, table(brain_section_label, neurotransmitter))
```

The table shows how many cells each combination contributes. Filters can be
applied when loading, as in `load_data("Zhuang4", filters = filters)`, or
when planning and fetching, as below. `load_data()` also accepts `cell_ids`
for an exact set of cell labels, and `n_cells` with `seed` for a
reproducible random sample of the selected cells.

Genes are selected with `genes`. Each entry is matched first against
`gene_identifier`, then against the published source identifier, then
against `gene_symbol`, so symbols and identifiers can be mixed. Three genes
below are given by symbol and Rxrg by its Ensembl identifier:

```{r gene-selection}
genes <- c("Htr7", "Sema3c", "Itga8", "ENSMUSG00000015843")
is_requested <- abc$gene_data$gene_symbol %in% genes |
    abc$gene_data$gene_identifier %in% genes
abc$gene_data[is_requested, c("gene_identifier", "gene_symbol")]
```

A symbol shared by several genes is reported as ambiguous, with a request
for the canonical identifier, rather than resolved silently.

# Planning the download

Expression files can be several gigabytes, so `plan_fetch()` reports what a
request needs before anything is downloaded. It takes the same selection as
`fetch_data()`:

```{r plan-fetch}
plan <- plan_fetch(abc, filters = filters, genes = genes)
plan
plan$approved
```

The plan lists the release, the representation, the number of selected genes
and cells, and each expression file involved, with its size, whether it is
already cached, any partial download that can be resumed, and the additional
download required. It also checks that the cache directory has enough free
disk space.

In an interactive session, `plan_fetch()` prints this plan and asks
`Proceed with download? [y/n]:`. Answering `y` approves the plan, and
`fetch_data(plan = plan)` then downloads and reads exactly what was planned
without asking again. Answering `n` leaves the plan unapproved, and
`fetch_data(plan = plan)` refuses to run. Use `confirm = FALSE` to skip the
question.

This vignette is built non-interactively, so no question is asked and the
plan stays unapproved (`NA` above). The next section therefore calls
`fetch_data()` with the same arguments instead of with the plan. A plan that
needs no download is approved automatically, as
[Reusing downloaded data](#reusing-downloaded-data) shows.

# Fetching expression

`fetch_data()` downloads the expression files the selection needs, then reads
only the selected cells and genes:

```{r fetch-matrix}
x <- fetch_data(
    abc,
    filters = filters,
    genes = genes,
    return_type = "matrix" # could pick "sce" or "spatial"
)
dim(x$expression)
x$expression[, 1:3]
Matrix::rowSums(x$expression > 0)
x$provenance
```

Rows are genes, keyed by `gene_identifier`, and columns are cells.
`Matrix::rowSums(x$expression > 0)` counts the selected cells in which each
gene is detected.

Only one expression file was downloaded. The ABC Atlas publishes each
expression matrix as a separate file per representation, and `Zhuang4`
defaults to `raw`. Setting `data_type = "log2"` would download the separate
upstream log2 file instead (about 107 MB for this route). Within the chosen
file, only the selected cells and genes are read into memory.

# Output types

`return_type` selects the representation returned by `fetch_data()`:

-   `"matrix"` (the default) returns a list with the sparse `expression`
    matrix, the selected `cell_metadata` and `gene_data`, the `data_type`
    and the `provenance` shown above. It needs no analysis framework.
-   `"sce"` returns a `SingleCellExperiment`. Raw expression is stored in a
    `counts` assay and upstream log2 expression in a `log2` assay. The
    provenance is stored in the object metadata.
-   `"spatial"` returns a `SpatialExperiment` with spatial coordinates
    attached. Coordinates are inferred automatically only for routes declared
    spatial, such as `Zhuang4`. For other metadata, verified coordinate
    columns must be named with `coordinate_columns`, so that
    dimensionality-reduction coordinates are never presented as physical
    locations.

Seurat and Monocle 3 objects are not built by `ABCatlas`, which keeps its
dependencies small. Both can be created from the matrix output with the
packages that define them. Both tools expect count data, so use raw
expression; `x` above is raw because raw is the default for `Zhuang4`.
`r CRANpkg("SeuratObject")` is on CRAN; `monocle3` is installed from GitHub.

```{r convert-seurat-monocle3, eval=FALSE}
# Seurat: Seurat replaces "_" in feature names, so rename them first.
counts <- x$expression
rownames(counts) <- gsub("_", "-", rownames(counts))
seu <- SeuratObject::CreateSeuratObject(
    counts = counts,
    meta.data = x$cell_metadata
)

# Monocle 3: gene metadata need a gene_short_name column.
gene_metadata <- x$gene_data
gene_metadata$gene_short_name <- gene_metadata$gene_symbol
cds <- monocle3::new_cell_data_set(
    x$expression,
    cell_metadata = x$cell_metadata,
    gene_metadata = gene_metadata
)
```

# Reusing downloaded data

Every downloaded file is recorded in the cache and reused by later requests,
including requests from new R sessions. Planning the same request again now
shows that nothing needs to be downloaded, so the plan is approved
automatically:

```{r reuse-plan}
plan_again <- plan_fetch(abc, filters = filters, genes = genes)
plan_again$total_download
plan_again$approved
```

Because it is approved, the plan can be passed to `fetch_data()`. The
expression file is read from the cache, and the message reports that no
download was needed:

```{r reuse-fetch}
x_again <- fetch_data(plan = plan_again)
identical(x$expression, x_again$expression)
```

Other datasets use the same cache. `HMBA_PatchSeq` is a small Patch-seq
dataset from the macaque basal ganglia. It is not spatial and is published
only as `log2` expression, which therefore becomes its default
representation:

```{r second-dataset}
patch_seq <- load_data("HMBA_PatchSeq")
patch_seq
```

```{r second-fetch}
y <- fetch_data(patch_seq, genes = c("GAD1", "PPP1R1B", "DRD1", "DRD2"))
dim(y$expression)
y$data_type
```

Its files are added to the cache next to those of `Zhuang4`, which remain
available. Cached files are reused by default. `offline = TRUE`, accepted by
`load_data()`, `plan_fetch()` and `fetch_data()`, additionally forbids
network access: for example, `load_data("Zhuang4", offline = TRUE)` now runs
without a connection, and a file that is not cached becomes an error instead
of a download.

# Cache location and releases

The cache directory is resolved in this order:

1.  the `download_base` argument of `load_data()`, `plan_fetch()`,
    `fetch_data()` or `abc_cache_connect()`;
2.  `options(ABCatlas.download_base = ...)`, as used in this vignette;
3.  the `ABC_ATLAS_CACHE` environment variable;
4.  a per-user cache directory, `tools::R_user_dir("ABCatlas", "cache")`.

In your own analyses, point the cache at a disk with enough free space;
files are then reused across R sessions. Metadata files are small, but the
expression files of a large dataset can take several gigabytes. Only the
files a request needs are downloaded, and interrupted downloads resume where
they stopped.

The files this vignette has cached so far:

```{r cache-contents}
list.files(abc_download_dir(), recursive = TRUE)
```

The package is release-aware. Each function uses the ABC Atlas release
validated against this version of the package unless another `release`
(in `YYYYMMDD` form) is given, so an analysis can be pinned to one release
for reproducibility. `abc_cache_connect()` gives lower-level access to the
files of a release manifest:

```{r cache-connect}
cache <- abc_cache_connect()
cache
```

`cache$get_file_path()` returns the local path of a manifest file,
downloading it only when it is not already cached and the cache is not
offline.

# Session information

```{r session-info}
sessionInfo()
```
